solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Is in control of distant armies abroad

indicators.note: abroad suggests being scattered far and wide, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A general directs forces stationed in far-off foreign lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges the thirteen letters of DISTANT and ARMIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer something is to manage it, so one who administrates is in charge of it.

clue.text: Plunder piled so haphazardly

indicators.note: haphazardly means in a random, disordered way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Loot has been stacked up any old how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haphazardly' rearranges the letters of PILED and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to strip of valuables by force, a verb synonym of plunder.

clue.text: Country artist with an outstanding level of intelligence

indicators.note: read as out-standing: the letters for intelligence stand outside, around the artist

parts.note: IQ, intelligence quotient, is a measured level of intelligence
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's standard artist

explanation.surface: A nation boasts a painter of exceptional brainpower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' seems to praise the intelligence, but it tells you IQ stands outside RA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation whose capital is Baghdad.

clue.text: Concentrated in time for a grammar lesson

parts.note: taken as written
a tense is the grammatical marking of time, such as past or future

explanation.surface: A pupil focuses hard during a lesson on grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means strong or highly focused, as concentrated flavour or effort is.

clue.text: Peter scrambled round to the highest branches

indicators.note: round means the scrambled name goes around the next small word
scrambled means mixed up, so the five letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Peter clambered up into the top of the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' turns the name into TREEP, and 'round' wraps those letters about the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: The topmost part of a tree is where its highest branches are.

clue.text: Freight unopened in Jason's ship

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: cargo is goods carried as freight

explanation.surface: Goods sealed and stowed aboard a famous ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' removes the first letter of CARGO. In Greek myth Jason sailed with the Argonauts in search of the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Argo carried Jason and his crew on the Golden Fleece quest.

clue.text: A high spot for the first mate, and others

parts.note: in Genesis Eve was the first wife, Adam's mate
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A mountaineer's summit party: the first mate and the remaining climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first mate' suggests a ship's officer, but it is Adam's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest mountain is literally a high spot.

clue.text: Down with psittacosis?

parts.note: down means depressed; psittacosis is a disease caught from parrots, so a parrot with it would be literally ill

explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for feeling bitterly disappointed, here taken literally of an ailing bird.

clue.text: They're not the type to settle for a band

definitions.text: They're not the type to settle
definitions.meaning: from the proverb about a moving stone gathering no moss: restless people who never settle down
a famous British rock group formed in the 1960s

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names wanderers in the proverb and also a famous rock band.

clue.text: A second coffee maybe

definitions.meaning: powdered coffee made by dissolving in water is this kind

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a moment and also describes quick-dissolving coffee.

clue.text: Attic studio ideal for this artist?

definitions.text: Attic studio ideal for this artist?

parts.words: Attic studio ideal for this artist?
parts.note: Attic means of Athens, Greek; the painter's nickname meant the Greek, so a Greek studio would suit him

explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan-born painter in Spain was known by a Spanish nickname meaning the Greek.

clue.text: Boss sounds a toff

indicators.note: sounds says the word for a toff is heard, not seen

parts.note: nob is British slang for an upper-class person, a toff

explanation.surface: The boss comes across as an upper-class snob.
explanation.walkthrough: A boss is a round knob, as on a shield. A toff is a posh person in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised stud or round protuberance, like a door knob.

clue.text: University can reject English couple

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the word for can is read in reverse

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A university may refuse to accept an English pair of students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reject' turns TIN into NIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple things is to join them together, a verb synonym.

clue.text: One who refused to accept tyranny and work in a bank

definitions.text: One who refused to accept tyranny
definitions.meaning: William ..., the Swiss hero who defied the tyrant Gessler
to count money, as a bank teller does

explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss folk hero bears the name, and the verb means to count, as bank tellers do.

clue.text: A poem of positive significance as a rule

definitions.text: of positive significance as a rule

parts.note: the article a becomes an before a vowel
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A verse written to carry an optimistic message, as is customary.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole tail of the clue: an electrode that is, by convention, the positive one.
explanation.definitionFit: In electrolysis the anode is conventionally the positively charged electrode.

clue.text: The offence of one coming to light

definitions.text: The offence of one coming to light

parts.words: The offence of one coming to light
parts.note: read as the crime of someone setting things alight, not of a fact being revealed

explanation.definitionFit: The crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: The peace subsequently broken by the French

indicators.note: broken by means the word for subsequently is split open with the next piece inside

parts.note: since means subsequently, as in ever since
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Later on, the calm was shattered by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: The French definite article is the inserted piece; 'broken by' says it splits the word for subsequently.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace in the sense of quiet is silence.

clue.text: Strait-laced girl enters into the joke

indicators.note: enters into means the girl's name goes inside the word for the joke

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A prim young woman joins in the fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strait-laced' is an adjective here, as the answer is used of prim behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A puritan person is morally strict and prudish, so strait-laced is an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Notice cut out and displayed

indicators.note: out here means outside: the word for cut goes around the notice

parts.note: pared means cut or trimmed
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: An announcement was clipped and put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' says PARED stands outside AD: PAR-AD-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade something is to show it off, so paraded means displayed.

clue.text: Its root may be made into a stew

indicators.note: may be made into says the letters are refashioned into something new

explanation.surface: A root vegetable can be turned into a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be made into' rearranges the letters of ITS and ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked in stock, loosely a stew.

clue.text: Women's work for girl employees

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name
staff are the employees

explanation.surface: Female labour done by the young woman's workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: A distaff is the stick used in spinning, traditionally women's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning stick came to stand for women's domestic tasks and the female side.

clue.text: Store up trouble for travelling performers

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Laying in supplies leads to difficulties for touring entertainers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges STORE and UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Troupes are companies of actors or performers, often touring.

clue.text: Ran round in the commotion caused by a storm

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for commotion

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion

indicators.note: round suggests turning about, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ran about in the chaos that a storm brought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges RAN into RNA, and 'in' sets it inside the fuss word; 'caused by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirling storm.

clue.text: Card game — bridge perhaps?

definitions.meaning: the British name for the card game twenty-one or blackjack
a floating bridge is supported on these flat boats

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a card game and a boat supporting a floating bridge.

clue.text: Wine for lady with an accent?

definitions.meaning: with an accent on the E the word is pink wine

explanation.walkthrough: 'with an accent' says the lady's name becomes the wine once an accent is added to its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is a girl's name, and with an acute accent it names pink wine.

clue.text: Too much interest is shown in it

definitions.text: Too much interest is shown in it

parts.words: Too much interest is shown in it
parts.note: reads like nosiness, but the interest is the charge on a loan

explanation.definitionFit: Lending money at excessive rates of interest.

clue.text: Free from any sound of disturbance

indicators.note: from tells you the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Somewhere peaceful, untroubled by any noise or interruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' reads as an adjective but defines a verb, to release or untie. 'any' and 'disturbance' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or fastening is to free or loosen it.

clue.text: Eager to behead the king of Israel

indicators.note: to behead is to cut off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: David was the biblical king of Israel

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to execute the Israelite monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behead' removes the first letter of DAVID.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen or enthusiastic, an adjectival synonym of eager.

clue.text: Wooden support for the shaft

definitions.meaning: a long timber holding up a structure

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a structural timber and a ray of light.

clue.text: A short month on a Roman road for Antony's wife

parts.note: Oct is the short form of October
via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

explanation.surface: Mark Antony's wife spent a brief month on a Roman highway.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' is the article; the second 'a' gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavia, sister of Octavian, was married to Mark Antony.

clue.text: Name one variety of flower

indicators.note: variety of means a varied form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Identify one kind of bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges NAME into ANEM; ONE stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant of the buttercup family with bright cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: It's said to get things done in the army

definitions.text: It's said to get things done in the army

parts.words: It's said to get things done in the army
parts.note: an order spoken aloud on parade by an officer to make soldiers act

explanation.definitionFit: An oral military order, such as one barked on the parade ground.
